oneLiner: Closed at 7,659.44 Friday, down 1.09% on the day and 1.95% on the week, about 2.0% below the record close of 7,818.93 set on October 6.
intro: The S&P 500 closed at 7,659.44 on Friday, October 16, down 1.09% on the day and about 1.95% on the week, after the prior week's gain. That leaves the index roughly 2.0% below its record close of 7,818.93 from October 6. A slightly hotter-than-expected inflation report and a slide in AI-linked technology shares were among the themes of the pullback.

performance.heading: How the index has done
performance.body: The strip above shows SPY giving back ground this week after last week's push toward records. The index itself lost about 1.95% over the five sessions, and more than half of that drop came on Friday, when AI-linked technology shares fell hard. The cards above track the same swings on SPY, so readings there may differ slightly from the index figures here.

chart.heading: The trend against its moving averages
chart.body: The index slid away from its record this week, a shift that may matter to chart watchers. The chart above plots SPY against its own moving-average lines over the same stretch, so the exact positions there may differ a little from the index figures quoted here.

levels.heading: Where the nearby levels sit
levels.body: The October 6 record close of 7,818.93 is the nearest marker above, about 2.1% higher than Friday's close. Below, the index's recent trading range may be what watchers look at next. The Price zones and Key levels cards above show where those levels sit on SPY today.

signals.heading: Momentum in plain words
signals.body: Momentum cooled during the week as the index slid from near its record. The weakness was concentrated in AI-linked technology, with chip stocks and the Nasdaq Composite hit hardest on Friday. The panel above shows today's RSI and MACD readings on SPY, which may help show how far that momentum has faded.

change.heading: The weekly and monthly pattern
change.body: Close to close, the index fell about 1.95% this week, after last week's gain, and now sits roughly 2.0% under its record. The index was almost flat on Tuesday, drifted lower through midweek and then dropped 1.09% on Friday as technology shares sank.

marketRead: The S&P 500 ended the week at 7,659.44, down 1.95% and about 2.0% below its October 6 record close of 7,818.93. It began the week near that high, closing at 7,805.45 on Tuesday, October 13. Inflation was the first test: on Wednesday, October 14, September consumer prices rose 3.7% from a year earlier, a little hotter than expected, with gasoline up 9.1% on the month, adding to worries that the Fed's September rate rise may not be the last.

Treasury yields were a focus after the CPI report, and the 10-year was near 5.1% on Friday. Market-implied odds of an October rate rise were about 16% on Friday, according to CME FedWatch, well below their midweek peak, after Kevin Warsh declined to hint at the coming decision in remarks at the IMF meetings in Bangkok on October 16.

Friday brought the week's sharpest damage. The Nasdaq Composite dropped 2.14% and chip stocks fell sharply as worries about AI spending and debt returned, with more than $50 billion of CoreWeave debt in focus. Energy shares rose as crude oil climbed, while the Dow slipped just 0.34% as investors leaned toward larger, more defensive names.

About 52% of S&P 500 members were above their 200-day average and 45% above their 50-day average at Friday's close, according to ChartRow. The optimistic case is that yields sit near 5.1% and October hike odds have fallen from their midweek peak. The cautious case is that the index has slid from its record, inflation is re-accelerating and AI-led leadership may stay fragile. The coming weeks may hinge on the Fed's October 27-28 meeting and company earnings.

points.label: Catalyst
points.text: Hotter September CPI (3.7% a year) on Wednesday, then a Friday slide in AI-linked tech, weighed on the index.

points.label: Breadth
points.text: About 52% of S&P 500 members were above their 200-day average at Friday's close, and 45% above their 50-day average.

points.label: Rates
points.text: The 10-year yield was near 5.1% on Friday; CME FedWatch put October rate-hike odds near 16%.

watchDown: The index extends this week's retreat from the October 6 record close of 7,818.93.
AI-linked technology shares extend Friday's slide, with debt worries around CoreWeave spreading wider.
Hot inflation data revives rate-hike bets ahead of the Fed's October 27-28 meeting.
Oil prices climb further, keeping inflation and Treasury yields elevated.
watchUp: The index recovers this week's losses and heads back toward the October 6 record close of 7,818.93.
The 10-year Treasury yield eases from about 5.1% as October hike bets stay subdued.
Company earnings show AI spending paying off, calming this week's valuation worries.
Breadth holds near half of members above their 200-day average even as technology wobbles.
